extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (postdocs and junior professors with temporary contracts) seeking Emmy Noether funding in Germany
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a proposal to the DFG Emmy Noether Programme to lead an independent junior research group and qualify for a university professorship. Includes eligibility, proposal content, required forms, funding modules, and procedural timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: To give highly qualified researchers the opportunity to satisfy the prerequisites for appointment as a university professor by leading an independent junior research group and performing relevant teaching duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programme aims to attract outstanding early career researchers (back) to Germany from abroad; funding objective is qualification-for-professorship via independent group leadership and teaching experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target group — career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career researchers in all disciplines, normally up to 4 years after completion of the doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should be at an early stage in their research careers; further eligibility details (postdoctoral experience, international experience) apply. The programme is not open to those who already satisfy professorship requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral experience requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally at least two years of postdoctoral experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a typical expectation for applicants; exceptions are not described on the page and applicants should consult programme contacts or guidelines if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: International research experience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International experience is expected as part of the applicant profile; this is part of the eligibility assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation for applicants from abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants from abroad are expected to continue their research careers in Germany after the funding comes to an end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programme seeks to attract or bring back researchers to Germany; continuation of career in Germany is an expectation tied to the funding objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of intent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A written letter of intent must be attached to the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory attachment to the proposal; refer to the forms and guidelines for templates and content expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — candidates who already satisfy professorship requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The ENP is not open to those who have already satisfied the requirements for a professorship, in particular those who have completed or are about to embark on the habilitation process. Holders of a junior professorship with a positive interim evaluation are no longer included in the target group for this programme, and are not eligible to submit proposals or receive funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant has effectively already achieved the programme's objective (qualification for professorship), they are ineligible. Check career status carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — concurrent similar funding
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual is not eligible if they are in receipt of a type of funding similar to the ENP for an independent (junior) research group from a national research institution, programmes offered by the federal and state governments, or an international institution located in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must not already hold funding that would duplicate ENP support for independent/junior research group leadership; clarify overlaps before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal requirement — excellent research project
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal must present an excellent research project; see full programme guidelines for expectations on scientific quality, scope, and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application evaluation — prior research and publication record
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessed on the basis of previous research work, ambitious publications in internationally respected journals or a comparable format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant track record (research outputs/publications) is a central element of evaluation. 'Ambitious publications' and internationally respected outlets or comparable formats are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic impact and mitigation (review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may address the impact of the pandemic as well as strategies for coping with it in the research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information will be taken into account on a subject-specific as well as on an individual level in the review and decision-making process — include relevant context about delays, interruptions, or mitigation strategies in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms, templates and guidelines requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All guidelines, templates and further forms for this programme can be found in the forms and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official DFG forms and templates (e.g., Form 50.02 'Emmy Noether-Programme') when preparing the application; follow formatting and content instructions in those documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding modules available
rubrics_metrics.description: Modules: Emmy Noether Group Leader; Basic Module; Temporary Substitutes for Clinicians; Mercator Fellows; Project-Specific Workshops; Public Relations; Family Allowance; Standard Allowance for Gender Equality Measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the detailed module descriptions in the programme guidelines to request appropriate budget lines and justify module use in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard funding period for an Emmy Noether independent junior research group is six years; plan project timeline and milestones accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timeline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow around eight months from submission to decision in planning career moves and commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing / deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals may be submitted at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rolling submissions are accepted; applicants should still allow for the decision timeline and coordinate with host institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with Collaborative Research Centres (CRCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Emmy Noether independent junior research group can be associated with a Collaborative Research Centre with a related topic at the same location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Association allows integration into an excellent research environment; as a full member of the CRC, the junior group leader shares in centralised funds. Consider CRC association when planning host environment and resource justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and procedural guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The department responsible for the relevant specialist area at the DFG Head Office will answer questions about submitting a proposal; procedural questions can be directed to procedures-researchcareers@dfg.de.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct programme-specific and procedural queries to the listed contacts; allow time for responses and consult FAQs and info talks linked on the programme page.
